:::{#rem-smooth-function-loose}
#### "Smooth" in statistics and machine learning

Statistics and machine learning texts often use "smooth" loosely,
for a function with as many [derivatives](#def-derivative) as the reasoning at hand needs,
usually two.
For example, a [cubic](algebra-exponentials.qmd#def-cubic-polynomial) spline,
a curve made of [polynomial](algebra-exponentials.qmd#def-polynomial) pieces of [degree](algebra-exponentials.qmd#def-polynomial-degree) $3$ that meet at knots
with matching first and [second derivatives](#def-second-derivative),
is called smooth,
although its third derivative jumps at each knot,
so it is not smooth in the sense of @def-smooth-function.
When a claim depends on the number of derivatives,
name that number ("twice-differentiable") rather than saying "smooth".

:::
